metadata.title: Top US Finance News
metadata.ranking_basis: Ranked by market impact and breadth of coverage on October 8, 2026. Rank 1 is the index close; ranks 2 and 3 are the two drivers named in the closing reports (the OpenAI revenue report and the oil jump); then rates (30-year auction, mortgage rates), the day's largest earnings report (PepsiCo), economic data (jobless claims), a Federal Reserve speech, crypto, and a single-stock analyst move.
metadata.fact_check_method: Researched by web search, then every story was re-checked against its sources in a second pass; facts and stories the re-check could not support were removed.

verification_status_legend.verified: Key facts confirmed by a primary source or by two or more independent sources
verification_status_legend.partially_verified: Core event confirmed, but one or more specific figures rest on a single source or sources conflict

limitations: Compiled by the pipeline's news step by web search.
Research was done about 45 minutes after the 4:00 PM ET close, so some figures are closing snapshots rather than final settlements; the notes on each story say which.
CNBC, Bloomberg and TheStreet pages returned access errors and could not be opened. Index closes were confirmed from Yahoo Finance and the AP index table instead.
The Labor Department's jobless claims PDF could not be read, so the claims figures rest on three secondary sources that agree (Haver Analytics, Investing.com, Yahoo Finance).
No Treasury primary page was opened for the 30-year auction; its figures come from three auction-tracking sites that agree with each other.
The Financial Times article on OpenAI's revenue was not opened directly; the story relies on two Yahoo Finance articles reporting it.
Closing prices for individual stocks (PepsiCo, Palantir, Oracle) were not confirmed and are left out; the Nvidia and Intel percentages are from Yahoo Finance's 4:04 PM update only.
The Waller speech story rests on one reference, the Federal Reserve Board's own speech text, which is the primary source; a search for same-day news coverage of the speech found none.
The reported SpaceX $40 billion debt raise was excluded because the report was first published on October 6, not October 8.
A search result said mortgage rates were the highest since November 2023; this was not confirmed on a page I opened and is not included.
Delta Air Lines reports on October 9, so it is not included.
'Bitcoin fell to about $80,000, a one-month low, as crypto liquidations neared $1 billion.': removed 1 key fact(s) the re-check could not support.

stories.headline: The S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 7,765.36 and the Nasdaq dropped 345.35 points while the Dow edged up 51.77 points to 51,231.64.
stories.summary: US stocks closed mixed on Thursday, October 8, 2026. The S&P 500 lost 36.41 points to 7,765.36, its second straight loss after setting an all-time high, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 345.35 points to 27,193.34. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 51.77 points to 51,231.64 and the Russell 2000 gained 0.92 point to 2,794.13. Reports attributed the weakness to a chip-stock selloff after a report on OpenAI's revenue and to a jump in oil prices that revived inflation worries.
key_facts: The S&P 500 fell 36.41 points, or 0.5% (0.47%), to close at 7,765.36.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 51.77 points, or 0.1%, to close at 51,231.64.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 345.35 points, or 1.3% (1.25%), to close at 27,193.34.
The Russell 2000 rose 0.92 point, less than 0.1%, to close at 2,794.13.
It was the S&P 500's second straight loss after setting an all-time high.
For the year, the S&P 500 is up 919.86 points, or 13.4%.
For the year, the Nasdaq is up 3,951.35 points, or 17%, and the Dow is up 3,168.35 points, or 6.6%.

fact_check.notes: Closing levels and point moves match on Yahoo Finance's live report (updated 4:04 PM EDT) and the AP 'How major US stock indexes fared' table. The Nasdaq percentage is 1.25% on Yahoo and rounded to 1.3% by AP; the S&P 500 is 0.47% on Yahoo and 0.5% in AP. A search snippet that showed the Russell 2000 down 38.77 points was its weekly move, not the daily one.

stories.headline: Chip and AI stocks sold off after the Financial Times reported OpenAI's annualized revenue is about $50 billion, roughly $20 billion below earlier estimates.
stories.summary: The Financial Times reported on October 8 that OpenAI's annualized revenue was roughly $50 billion as of September, about $20 billion below the $70 billion figure that had been widely reported. The gap came from investors adjusting OpenAI's numbers to match how Anthropic counts sales through cloud partners. AI-linked stocks fell on the report: Oracle dropped more than 5% during the session, and Nvidia and Intel ended lower.
key_facts: The Financial Times reported OpenAI's annualized revenue was roughly $50 billion as of September.
That is about $20 billion below the $70 billion figure previously estimated.
At $50 billion, OpenAI trails Anthropic's reported $65 billion in annualized sales.
Oracle shares dropped more than 5% during the session.
Nvidia fell 2.94% and Intel fell 5.34%, per Yahoo Finance's closing update.
Micron fell more than 5%, and Arm Holdings and Marvell Technology each fell more than 6%.
At a $1.4 trillion funding target, OpenAI would be valued at about 28 times annualized revenue.

fact_check.notes: The $50 billion, $70 billion and $20 billion figures are confirmed in two Yahoo Finance articles citing the Financial Times; the FT article itself was not opened. Individual stock percentages (Nvidia, Intel, Micron, Arm, Marvell) come from Yahoo Finance's live report only. The Oracle move of more than 5% was an intraday reading, not a confirmed close.

stories.headline: Brent crude jumped 4% to $104.28 a barrel as Iran stepped up tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz and Hurricane Isaias shut in Gulf output.
stories.summary: Oil prices rose sharply on Thursday. Brent crude gained 4% to close at $104.28 a barrel and US West Texas Intermediate rose 3.6% to $91.49. Nine tankers were attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz over the past week, and Hurricane Isaias led operators to shut in about 500,000 barrels per day of Gulf of Mexico production. Prices came off their highs, after rising more than 5%, when President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections.
key_facts: Brent crude rose 4% to close at $104.28 a barrel.
US West Texas Intermediate crude rose 3.6% to settle at $91.49 a barrel.
Nine tankers came under attack in and around the Strait of Hormuz over the past week.
Hurricane Isaias led oil companies to shut in about 500,000 barrels per day, or 25% of Gulf of Mexico production.
Oil had been up more than 5% before paring gains.
President Trump said: "We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections."
Regular gasoline averaged $4.36 per gallon and diesel $6.28 per gallon.

fact_check.notes: The $104.28 and $91.49 closes with 4% and 3.6% gains appear in NBC News and in CNBC's oil report (CNBC seen in search results only; the page returned an access error). Yahoo Finance's 4:04 PM snapshot showed WTI at $90.79 and Brent near $104, and Trading Economics showed $90.87 and $103.70; these are later electronic quotes, not settlements. The tanker and hurricane figures match on CNBC and Trading Economics. Gasoline and diesel averages are from NBC News only.

stories.headline: The Treasury sold $22 billion of 30-year bonds at a high yield of 5.618%, reported as the highest for that auction since August 2000.
stories.summary: The Treasury auctioned $22 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday at a high yield of 5.618%, up from 5.308% at the September sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.54 and indirect bidders took 72.3%. The 10-year Treasury yield stood at 5.23% and the 30-year at 5.61% late in the day.
key_facts: The Treasury sold $22 billion of 30-year bonds at a high yield of 5.618%.
The auction yield was reported as the highest since August 2000.
The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.54, against a recent average of 2.41.
Indirect bidders took 72.3% of the sale and direct bidders took 20.9%.
Primary dealers were left with 6.8%.
The high yield was 0.1 basis point above the when-issued level of 5.617%.
The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.23% and the 30-year yield was 5.61% in Yahoo Finance's closing update.

fact_check.notes: Auction size, yield, bid-to-cover and bidder shares agree across three auction-tracking sites (Helious, TFTC, investingLive), but no Treasury primary page or major news outlet was opened. The 'highest since August 2000' claim rests on TFTC and a search snippet. The September yield of 5.308% is from search results. The 10-year and 30-year closing yields are from Yahoo Finance only. The investingLive page showed a date of August 10, 2026, which appears to be a day/month misreading of 8/10.

stories.headline: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 7.40%, its seventh straight weekly increase.
stories.summary: Freddie Mac's weekly survey, released Thursday, showed the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaging 7.40%, up from 7.28% a week earlier and 6.30% a year ago. The 15-year fixed rate averaged 6.73%, up from 6.60%. It was the seventh consecutive weekly rise.
key_facts: The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 7.40% as of October 8, 2026.
The 30-year rate was 7.28% the week before and 6.30% a year ago.
The 15-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.73%, up from 6.60% the week before.
The 15-year rate was 5.53% a year ago.
Mortgage rates rose for the seventh consecutive week.

fact_check.notes: Rates confirmed on Freddie Mac's own survey page and in Fox Business. The seven-week streak is from Fox Business. A search-result claim that this is the highest since November 2023 was not confirmed and is left out.

stories.headline: PepsiCo reported third-quarter core earnings of $2.34 a share on revenue of $25.27 billion but cut its full-year profit outlook.
stories.summary: PepsiCo reported third-quarter 2026 results on Thursday. Net revenue rose 5.6% to $25.274 billion, organic revenue grew 3.1%, and core earnings per share rose 2% to $2.34. The company lowered its 2026 forecast for core constant-currency EPS growth to 1% to 2%, from the low end of 4% to 6%.
key_facts: PepsiCo's third-quarter net revenue was $25.274 billion, up 5.6%.
Organic revenue grew 3.1%.
Core earnings per share were $2.34, up 2%.
Reported earnings per share were $2.23, up 17%.
PepsiCo cut its 2026 core constant-currency EPS growth forecast to 1% to 2%, from the low end of 4% to 6%.
PepsiCo cut its 2026 core EPS growth forecast to 2.5% to 3.5%, from the low end of 5% to 7%.
PepsiCo Foods North America's core constant-currency operating profit fell 12%.
The quarter included $178 million of tariff refunds.

fact_check.notes: Revenue, EPS and guidance are from PepsiCo's earnings release filed with the SEC on October 8, 2026. The $178 million tariff refund figure is from Yahoo Finance and search-result summaries; the release was read as describing a 4-percentage-point benefit to core operating profit. Yahoo Finance's live report gave the new core EPS guidance as 2.5% to 3%; the SEC filing says 2.5% to 3.5% and is used here. The share-price reaction was not confirmed and is omitted.

stories.headline: Initial jobless claims slipped by 2,000 to 197,000 in the week ended October 3, below the 200,000 forecast.
stories.summary: The Labor Department reported Thursday that initial claims for unemployment benefits fell by 2,000 to 197,000 in the week ended October 3, below the 200,000 consensus. The four-week average fell to 198,000 from 200,500. Continuing claims rose by 17,000 to 1.716 million in the week ended September 26.
key_facts: Initial jobless claims fell by 2,000 to 197,000 in the week ended October 3.
Economists had expected 200,000.
The four-week moving average fell to 198,000 from 200,500.
Continuing claims rose by 17,000 to 1.716 million in the week ended September 26.
The insured unemployment rate held at 1.1%.

fact_check.notes: Figures agree across Haver Analytics, Investing.com and Yahoo Finance. The Labor Department's own PDF release could not be read, so no primary source was confirmed directly.

stories.headline: Fed Governor Waller said 16 of 18 policymakers expect at least one more rate hike this year after September's increase to 3.75% to 4%.
stories.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller spoke on the economic outlook on October 8 at the Istanbul Economic Forum. He noted that the FOMC raised its policy rate 25 basis points in September to 3.75% to 4% after holding it steady for nine months. He said 16 of the 18 participants who submitted projections anticipated at least one more hike in the two remaining meetings this year, and four of those expected two.
key_facts: Waller said the FOMC raised its policy rate 25 basis points in September to 3.75% to 4%.
The September hike came after nine months of holding the rate steady.
Sixteen of the 18 participants who submitted dots anticipated at least one more hike in the two remaining meetings this year.
Four of those 16 expected two additional hikes.
Waller said markets have interpreted that the Committee is likely to raise the policy rate 50 basis points in the coming months.
August core PCE inflation was 0.25% for the month and 3% over 12 months.

fact_check.notes: The one source is primary: the Federal Reserve Board's own published text of the speech, dated October 8, 2026, at the Istanbul Economic Forum. Every key fact was re-read against that text and matches it. A search for same-day news coverage of the speech found no second source, so there is one reference only. The delivery time in US Eastern time was not checked.

references.title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook

stories.headline: Bitcoin fell to about $80,000, a one-month low, as crypto liquidations neared $1 billion.
stories.summary: Bitcoin dropped to roughly $80,000 on Thursday, its lowest level in about a month, according to CoinDesk. It was down about 4% over 24 hours and more than 8% from near $87,000 four days earlier. Ether and XRP each fell roughly 6% and Solana about 9%. Liquidations across crypto totaled $974 million over 24 hours.
key_facts: Bitcoin fell to about $80,000, its lowest level in about a month.
Bitcoin was down about 4% over 24 hours and more than 8% from nearly $87,000 four days earlier.
Ether and XRP each fell roughly 6% and Solana fell about 9%.
Crypto liquidations totaled $974 million over 24 hours.

fact_check.notes: Crypto trades around the clock, so prices depend on the time of the snapshot: CoinDesk reported a low near $80,000 and a 4% 24-hour drop, while Yahoo Finance showed $81,750.10, down 1.96%, at 4:04 PM. The $974 million liquidation figure is from Yahoo Finance; a second outlet (Invezz, search result only) described liquidations as nearly $1 billion. The altcoin percentages are from CoinDesk only. Re-check: CoinDesk (October 8, 2:14 p.m. EDT) confirms bitcoin at about $80,000, a one-month low, down 4% in 24 hours and more than 8% from nearly $87,000 four days earlier, with ether and XRP down about 6% and Solana 9%. Yahoo Finance confirms $974 million in liquidations. Yahoo's closing update, however, shows bitcoin at $81,694.72, down 2.03%, on two separate reads. The file's $81,750.10 and -1.96% do not match the cited source.

references.title: Bitcoin price news: BTC falls to $80,000 nearly one year after October 2025 crash

stories.headline: Palantir rose about 3% after Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to Buy with a $230 price target.
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges upgraded Palantir Technologies to Buy from Neutral on Thursday and set a $230 price target. Palantir shares climbed about 3% in morning trading, against a weaker tech market. Goldman cited about $8 billion in annual recurring revenue with growth near 100%, and rising demand for sovereign AI.
key_facts: Goldman Sachs upgraded Palantir to Buy from Neutral with a $230 price target.
Palantir shares rose about 3% on Thursday morning.
The analyst is Gabriela Borges.
Goldman cited about $8 billion in annual recurring revenue with growth near 100%.
Palantir trades at roughly 160 times earnings, per The Motley Fool.

fact_check.notes: The upgrade, the $230 target and the roughly 3% gain are confirmed by The Motley Fool and Yahoo Finance's live report. The 3% gain is a morning reading; the closing move was not confirmed, and one search result said the stock retreated from its highs. The valuation multiple is from The Motley Fool only.
